findings.component: primary_filing — Application to Expunge the Record of a Conditional Discharge, Miss. Code Ann. § 41-29-150(d)(2)
findings.defect: Page 4 of the assembled packet ends on the bare bold heading VERIFICATION. Its statement — "Petitioner states that the facts set out above are true and correct to the best of Petitioner's knowledge and belief. This is a simple statement of truth. No Mississippi statute reached by this petition requires it to be sworn or notarized, and no notarial block is printed here." — and the signature rule, the printed name and the address that follow it all begin on page 5. The heading is stranded from the section it names, and a reader turning the page meets a signature rule whose heading is on the sheet behind it. This is the only page in the family where it happens: the paraphernalia variant carries the heading and the first line of the statement together, and on both ms-dui and both ms-mip packets the heading and the whole statement sit on one page. Which fixture is hit is a function of how much text precedes the block, so this is pagination-dependent rather than fixture-specific.
findings.origin: Shared renderer, not fixture data and not the Mississippi module. src/lib/rcap/packets/engines/custom-pleading.ts writes the VERIFICATION heading, a half-line gap and the verification text as three independent writes with no keep-together guard, immediately before the execution block, which does have one and is measured and moved as a unit. Commit 43570e0 added a keep-together rule for template section headings; the verification heading is not a template section heading and was not covered by it.
findings.verifierGap: The committed verifier's stranded-heading assertion, at scripts/verify-rcap-mississippi-custom-pleading.mjs lines 1135-1149, tests the last written line of each page against headingLines(template), which is built only from template.sections[].heading. VERIFICATION is emitted by the engine rather than declared as a section, so it is outside the assertion's denominator and the verifier reports "no heading stranded from its section" while this page ends on one. The assertion is not wrong, its denominator is incomplete.
findings.expectedTreatment: The verification heading, the verification statement and the execution block below them should move together, the way the execution block already does — measured and kept on one page rather than allowed to break between the heading and its text. The stranded-heading assertion should then be widened to cover engine-emitted headings, not only template section headings, so the guarantee the verifier prints is the guarantee it tests.
findings.correctionOwnerReason: The defect is in src/lib/rcap/packets/engines/custom-pleading.ts, the shared custom-pleading renderer, which no state implementation job owns. Under the correction-ownership rule a shared renderer or layout defect belongs to SESSION_A unless the live plan creates another exact owner, and the live plan creates none. Correcting it will change the assembled bytes of every custom-pleading family whose pagination is affected, so it is a shared change rather than a Mississippi change.
findings.supersedesNote: Any correction changes the assembled bytes of at least ms-drug-cd-conditional-discharge-possession-1, so data/record-clearing/production-factory/packet-proofs/rcap-ms-custom-pleading.json and data/record-clearing/production-factory/review-manifests/rcap-ms-custom-pleading.json must both be regenerated by SESSION_A before this family is reviewed again. Other custom-pleading families may need the same treatment.
findings.participantHarmNote: Nothing false is stated and no actor boundary is crossed. The cost is that the operative filing's verification reads as a heading with nothing under it, which is the kind of layout a clerk or a judge notices on a self-represented filing.
